status_summary: The OSTP Director also holds the title Assistant to the President for Science and Technology and co-chairs the President's Council of Advisors on Science and Technology under Executive Order 14177 (2025-01-23). OSTP and OMB issued joint R&D budget priority memoranda on 2025-09-23 (FY2027, five priority areas) and 2026-07-21 (FY2028, nine priority areas with named national missions in areas such as AI, quantum, fusion, space, robotics and semiconductors), and the FY2028 memo has larger R&D agencies send action plans to OSTP and OMB within 90 days. Neither memo uses the Industries of the Future label or states that it narrows that list, and no formal step raising the Director's standing was found.

timeline.event: Executive Order 14177 reestablished PCAST with the Assistant to the President for Science and Technology as a co-chair.

OSTP and OMB issued memorandum M-25-34 (NSTM-2) on FY2027 R&D budget priorities, naming five areas (critical and emerging technologies, energy, national security, health and biotechnology, space) and five cross-cutting actions.
OSTP and OMB issued memorandum M-26-16 on FY2028 R&D priorities, with nine priority areas, named national missions, and agency action plans due to OSTP and OMB within 90 days.

title: Elevate OSTP Director, lead federal R&D coordination, narrow Industries of the Future list
uncertainties: The memoranda's priority areas overlap with the earlier Industries of the Future topics, but whether they narrow that list is an inference; the FY2027 memo has five areas while the FY2028 memo has nine, so any narrowing is not consistent across years. The Director's standing relative to agencies could not be measured from public sources. The progress figure is an inference. Climate research restructuring is covered by c02-04.
